diagnostics.notes: Both claims verified against their abstracts. A: explicit statement that dapagliflozin did not lower systolic BP at 1 or 12 weeks vs placebo (sentence 9). B: between-group change in SBP of -3.7 mmHg favoring dapagliflozin at 12 weeks (sentence 11), with no significance wording reported. Same drug, dose, comparator, outcome, and time point; populations differ (kidney transplant recipients vs type 2 diabetes) but this does not block abstract-level comparison.

source_evidence.quote: Compared with placebo, dapagliflozin did not lower systolic BP at 1 or 12 weeks

After 12 weeks, patients randomized to dapagliflozin, as compared to those randomized to placebo, showed improvements in HbA1c (- 1.2%; 13 mmol/mol), systolic blood pressure (- 3.7 mmHg), and body weight (- 3.3 kg).

verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both are randomized placebo-controlled trials of dapagliflozin 10 mg for 12 weeks reporting systolic blood pressure as a between-group outcome. Study A (kidney transplant recipients) explicitly concludes no SBP lowering versus placebo at 1 or 12 weeks ('dapagliflozin did not lower systolic BP at 1 or 12 weeks'). Study B (type 2 diabetes) reports a directional between-group improvement in SBP of -3.7 mmHg with dapagliflozin versus placebo at 12 weeks. An explicit no-effect conclusion against a reported effect takes the not_replicated branch; the differing populations (KTR vs T2D) are contextual but no text-supported explanation is needed for this branch.
